complaint: This cover is not right: one side slopes down neatly, the other side stays straight. The daybed is the same on the left and the right.
cause: The cover was built with an uneven set of panels: on the right side there is an angled panel (normal 0.82, -0.57, 0.06), while the left side uses a straight vertical panel (normal -1, 0, 0) and a separate top slope (normal -0.2, -0.37, 0.91). The furniture is left-right symmetric, but the cover's panels are not mirror images, so one side slopes and the other stays straight.
rule: For furniture that is left-right symmetric, the cover must be left-right symmetric: every panel on one side must have an identical mirrored panel on the other side.
check: Mirror each panel's centre and normal across the furniture's left-right centre plane and verify that a matching panel with the same area exists within a small tolerance.

complaint: The top can be cut in one piece (the owner, 2 Oct 2026); it was 4 pieces with a 3.7 cm sliver.
cause: The box with 7 pieces was chosen for a tighter fit; its top became four faces, one only 37 mm wide, although the whole top lies flat about 1.2 m wide and fits the 1.48 m roll.
rule: Choose the box option with the fewest top pieces that fit the roll; never an option with a piece narrower than the minimum piece width (a sliver); more room round the furniture is a fair price for a top without seams.
check: The audit's slivers check (no piece narrower than seams.min_piece_width_mm) and its top pieces note.

complaint: You drew a sloping side instead of an L shape with a sharp corner; when generating these big covers the cover must follow the product and not draw diagonal lines (the owner, 7 Oct 2026).
cause: The box cover is the intersection of flat half-spaces, so it is always convex: over a chaise longue and a 2-seater placed as an L, the face that took away the most room was a slanted wall across the open inner corner, and one top spanned the whole L (1.66 m in its narrowest direction, over the roll).
rule: A cover over furniture placed together follows the pieces seen from above: their rectangles joined, right-angled inner corners, every wall straight down, nothing spanning an open corner; tops slope down to each piece's own front and pieces wider than the roll are split with seams running downhill. One rectangle round everything, or the smoothed outline, only when chosen on the page.
check: The audit's plan check (the cover within the pieces plus the clearance, seen from above) and the tests in engine/tests/test_arrange.py (an L gives an L with a sharp inner corner).

complaint: Crossed-out panels can become one panel (Rens, 8 Oct 2026; also the bar chairs, Vittoria, the corners Aspen, Avero and Emar, Monte Vari, Sato).
cause: A flat top is drained into a gable of two faces at the minimum slope (a 10 degree fold) and the box's face choice adds near-parallel faces (3 to 7 degrees); every flat face was its own piece.
rule: Neighbouring box faces on the same side that meet at a fold of at most seams.fold_join_max_deg lie flat together: one piece with a fold line, the gentlest fold first, while it fits the roll.
check: The audit's gentle folds check and engine/tests/test_facets.py (a gable top is one piece).

complaint: For the cut pieces please follow the lines of the original model (Rens, 8 Oct 2026; also S60).
cause: A given cover surface got the usual level skirt seam and a roll split; its own creases (the top's front and back edges) were ignored.
rule: A cover surface of its own is cut along its own creases sharper than seams.given_crease_deg; the pieces are what the creases enclose.
check: engine/tests/test_given_creases.py (a given surface with creases is cut on them).

complaint: The right number of vents, but too many at the back, the side not seen on the drawing: per back panel move one vent to the front, at the circles; all at the same height on the skirt, in the middle of the panels (Rens, 8 Oct 2026, 49 covers).
cause: The drawing's vent count was spread over the sides by length, so the long back walls got two or three and the front walls of an L, U or C (skipped as inner walls) none; a free top edge counted as hem and got a vent upside down; a box cover's low band got no vents at all.
rule: Vents go round every side of the cover, the seen front too: one in the middle of each piece first, a side not served yet before another piece facing the same way, extra ones on the longest pieces; the drawing's number kept; all at the bottom, never on a free top edge; a band too low for a vent hands it to the piece above.
check: The audit's vents check (count, every side served, none high up a wall) and scripts/fewer_check.py.

complaint: Make the cover round in top view, not square or octagonal; follow the (round, organic) outline of the furniture from the top view better (Rens at the Desk, 8 Oct 2026, on 18 round tables and 12 lounges).
cause: The box cover is an intersection of flat half-spaces: its plan is a convex polygon of a few straight sides, so a round table (with the chair ring round it) got a square or an octagon, and a kidney- or moon-shaped sofa a polygon over empty floor and across its bays.
rule: A box cover's plan comes from the furniture seen from above: when the footprint fills at least hull.round_fill of its smallest circle the cover is a round skirt with a cone on top resting on the support (water runs off, the skirt seam level, the top in equal sectors that fit the roll); when the box's straight sides stand more than hull.plan_follow_mm beyond the outline, the walls stand straight down on the outline (bays and inner corners rounded to hull.plan_round_mm) under the box's own top faces, which still span seats.
check: The audit's outline check (a box built where round or follow is due fails) and engine/tests/test_outline.py (a round table gets a round cover, a kidney sofa keeps its bay).

complaint: The marked part is empty space, make the cover smaller (Rens at the Desk, 8 Oct 2026, on six dining chairs).
cause: The word 'dining' in a chair's name made it a dining table: chair space (33 cm deep, 87 cm high) was added in front of and behind the chair, so the cover was twice as deep as the chair.
rule: Chair space only round a table: never round furniture named chair, stool, sofa or bench, and only when the table's top is at least hull.table_top_min_mm deep both ways (a chair's highest part is a backrest rail).
